title: RBI Governor Shaktikanta Das: Your Shield Against Digital Frauds
description: RBI Governor Shaktikanta Das recently issued a strong warning about the increasing threat of digital payment frauds. He urged banks and all citizens to be ext.

faq.q: What is the RBI's role in preventing digital fraud?
faq.a: The RBI sets regulations and guidelines for banks and payment systems to ensure their security, conducts public awareness campaigns like 'RBI Kehta Hai', and works with law enforcement agencies to combat financial crime.

faq.q: What should I do if I suspect I've been a victim of digital fraud?
faq.a: Immediately contact your bank's customer care, block your card/account if necessary, and report the incident to the National Cybercrime Helpline at 1930 or file a complaint on www.cybercrime.gov.in.

faq.q: Are banks responsible for all fraud losses?
faq.a: Not always. If you have been negligent (e.g., sharing OTPs), you might bear some or all of the loss. However, if the fraud is due to a bank's system failure or a third-party breach without your involvement, the bank is generally liable, provided you report it promptly.

faq.q: How can I stay updated on the latest fraud warnings?
faq.a: Regularly check the RBI's official website, follow their social media handles, and pay attention to messages from your bank. They often share warnings about new fraud techniques.

faq.q: Does the RBI Governor's statement mean new rules are coming?
faq.a: While this specific statement was an emphasis on vigilance, such strong messages from the Governor often signal areas of focus for future policy. The RBI continuously reviews and updates its regulations to enhance consumer protection.
